accepted.s: Who among the following rulers of the Shah Mir dynasty of Kashmir was known by the epithet “Butshikan”?
accepted.x: Sikandar, who ruled Kashmir from 1389 to 1413, was given the epithet “Butshikan”, meaning idol-breaker.
accepted.tq: Test the ruler–epithet association directly.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s: Sikandar Butshikan is associated with which of the following policies in Kashmir?
o: Destroying temples, imposing jizya and driving out Brahmins
accepted.x: Sikandar Butshikan destroyed temples, imposed jizya and drove out Brahmins. The other measures are associated with Zain-ul-Abidin.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–policy trap to distinguish two successive Kashmir rulers.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s: Zain-ul-Abidin, who ruled Kashmir from 1420 to 1470, was originally known as:
accepted.x: The original name of Zain-ul-Abidin was Shahi Khan.
accepted.tq: Separate a ruler’s original name from his regnal title and epithet.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir was popularly known by which of the following titles?
o: Bud Shah and the Akbar of Kashmir
Butshikan and Lord of the East
accepted.x: Zain-ul-Abidin was called “Bud Shah”, meaning Great King, and the “Akbar of Kashmir”.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler with his distinctive epithets, avoiding famous but unrelated titles.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious policy of Zain-ul-Abidin:
1. He abolished jizya.
2. He permitted the rebuilding of temples.
3. He called back Brahmins who had fled Kashmir.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the conciliatory religious policy of Zain-ul-Abidin.
accepted.tq: Recognise a cluster of measures belonging to the same ruler.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s:
Which of the following works were translated into Persian during the reign of Zain-ul-Abidin?
1. Mahabharata
2. Rajatarangini
3. Mirat-i-Sikandari
4. Riyaz-us-Salatin
accepted.x: The Mahabharata and Kalhana’s Rajatarangini were translated into Persian during Zain-ul-Abidin’s reign. The other two are later or unrelated works.
accepted.tq: Eliminate works belonging to other regional chronicles.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s: Who continued the Rajatarangini under the patronage of Zain-ul-Abidin?
accepted.x: Jonaraja continued the Rajatarangini during the reign of Zain-ul-Abidin.
accepted.tq: Test the author–continuation relationship rather than the original authorship.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched with reference to the works of Zain-ul-Abidin in Kashmir?
o: Zaina Lank — island in the Sabarmati
accepted.x: Zaina Kadal was a bridge constructed at Srinagar. Zaina Lank was an island in Wular Lake.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure location and distinguish Kashmir monuments from monuments of other regions.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s: Zaina Lank, associated with Zain-ul-Abidin, is located in:
accepted.x: Zaina Lank is an island in Wular Lake in Kashmir.
accepted.tq: Use the monument–geographical location association.
accepted.sec: Kashmir - Zain-ul-Abidin (name, epithets, religious policy, translations, monuments), Sikandar Butshikan

accepted.s: Who founded the Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur in 1394?
o: Malik Sarwar, also known as Khwaja Jahan
accepted.x: Malik Sarwar, known as Khwaja Jahan, founded the Sharqi dynasty in 1394 after receiving the title Malik-us-Sharq.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the founder of the dynasty from the founder of the city and its last ruler.
accepted.sec: Jaunpur - Sharqi dynasty, rulers, "Shiraz of India", monuments → builder (Atala Masjid)

accepted.s: Malik Sarwar, the founder of the Sharqi dynasty, was given which title?
accepted.x: Malik Sarwar received the title Malik-us-Sharq, meaning Lord of the East.
accepted.tq: Test the title associated with the correct founder.
accepted.sec: Jaunpur - Sharqi dynasty, rulers, "Shiraz of India", monuments → builder (Atala Masjid)

accepted.s: Jaunpur acquired the title “Shiraz-i-Hind” primarily because it was:
o: The capital of the Bahmani kingdom
accepted.x: Jaunpur was called Shiraz-i-Hind because it developed as a centre of learning.
accepted.tq: Link an honorific geographical title with the reason for its use.
accepted.sec: Jaunpur - Sharqi dynasty, rulers, "Shiraz of India", monuments → builder (Atala Masjid)

accepted.s: Which form of music received patronage at the Sharqi court of Jaunpur?
accepted.x: The Sharqi court patronised Khyal music.
accepted.tq: Test the court–cultural tradition association.
accepted.sec: Jaunpur - Sharqi dynasty, rulers, "Shiraz of India", monuments → builder (Atala Masjid)

accepted.s: Pir Bodhan, associated with the Sharqi court of Jaunpur, was a:
accepted.x: Pir Bodhan was a Sufi musician who flourished under Husain Shah Sharqi.
accepted.tq: Identify the person by profession and court association.
accepted.sec: Jaunpur - Sharqi dynasty, rulers, "Shiraz of India", monuments → builder (Atala Masjid)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events related to Jaunpur in chronological order:
A. Foundation of the Sharqi dynasty
B. Fall of Jaunpur to Bahlul Lodi
C. Founding of Jaunpur city by Firoz Shah Tughlaq
accepted.x: Jaunpur city was founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq before the Sharqi dynasty was founded in 1394; Jaunpur fell to Bahlul Lodi in 1479.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest city-foundation event and the final conquest before ordering the middle event.
accepted.sec: Jaunpur - Sharqi dynasty, rulers, "Shiraz of India", monuments → builder (Atala Masjid)

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Atala Masjid — Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
2. Jama Masjid, Jaunpur — Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
3. Lal Darwaza Mosque — Bibi Raje
4. Ashrafi Mahal — Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
accepted.x: Atala Masjid and Jama Masjid were associated with Ibrahim Shah Sharqi, while Lal Darwaza Mosque was built by Bibi Raje. Ashrafi Mahal belongs to Mandu, not Jaunpur.
accepted.tq: Use the monument–builder table and reject a monument shifted from another kingdom.
accepted.sec: Jaunpur - Sharqi dynasty, rulers, "Shiraz of India", monuments → builder (Atala Masjid)

accepted.s: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in which year?
accepted.x: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the foundation year from nearby dates of regional dynasties.
accepted.sec: Bahmani Sultanate - founder, capitals in order (Gulbarga, Bidar), wars with Vijayanagara (Raichur Doab)

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Bahmani Sultanate is correct?
1. It was the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan.
2. Gulbarga was its initial capital.
3. Its last Sultan was Kalimullah.
4. The kingdom ended in 1527.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Bahmani kingdom was founded in the Deccan, initially ruled from Gulbarga, and ended in 1527 under its last Sultan, Kalimullah.
accepted.tq: Check every statement against the kingdom’s identity, capital, last ruler and terminal date.
accepted.sec: Bahmani Sultanate - founder, capitals in order (Gulbarga, Bidar), wars with Vijayanagara (Raichur Doab)

accepted.s: Who built the Jama Masjid at Gulbarga?
accepted.x: The Jama Masjid at Gulbarga was built by Muhammad Shah I and has a fully covered courtyard.
accepted.tq: Use the builder–monument association and avoid confusing rulers of the Bahmani kingdom.
accepted.sec: Bahmani Sultanate - founder, capitals in order (Gulbarga, Bidar), wars with Vijayanagara (Raichur Doab)

accepted.s: Which Bahmani ruler was described as a scholar-king and is associated with the peak strength of the kingdom?
accepted.x: Firuz Shah, who ruled from 1397 to 1422, was regarded as a scholar-king and the Bahmani kingdom reached peak strength during his reign.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler with the distinctive characterization and reign period.
accepted.sec: Bahmani Sultanate - founder, capitals in order (Gulbarga, Bidar), wars with Vijayanagara (Raichur Doab)

accepted.s: The principal cause of the wars between the Bahmani Sultanate and Vijayanagara was control over the:
accepted.x: The Raichur Doab, also called Raichur Antarvedi, was the principal cause of conflict between the Bahmani Sultanate and Vijayanagara.
accepted.tq: Identify the principal disputed region rather than secondary contested zones.
accepted.sec: Bahmani Sultanate - founder, capitals in order (Gulbarga, Bidar), wars with Vijayanagara (Raichur Doab)

accepted.s:
Which of the following were also disputed zones in the Bahmani–Vijayanagara conflicts?
1. Krishna-Godavari delta
2. Marathwada
3. Mewar
4. Khandesh
accepted.x: The Krishna-Godavari delta and Marathwada were other disputed zones. Mewar and Khandesh are associated with other regional kingdoms in the period.
accepted.tq: Distinguish secondary disputed regions from territories belonging to other kingdoms.
accepted.sec: Bahmani Sultanate - founder, capitals in order (Gulbarga, Bidar), wars with Vijayanagara (Raichur Doab)

accepted.s: Who broke away from Delhi and established the Malwa kingdom in 1401?
accepted.x: Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi and established the independent Malwa kingdom in 1401.
accepted.tq: Separate the founder of independence from later rulers and builders.
accepted.sec: Malwa - rulers, Mandu monuments → builder (Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Jami Masjid), Baz Bahadur and Rupmati

accepted.s: Who shifted the capital of Malwa from Dhar to Mandu?
accepted.x: Hoshang Shah shifted the capital of Malwa from Dhar to Mandu.
accepted.tq: Test the ruler associated with a capital transfer.
accepted.sec: Malwa - rulers, Mandu monuments → builder (Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Jami Masjid), Baz Bahadur and Rupmati

accepted.s: The Khalji line of Malwa was founded by:
accepted.x: Mahmud Khalji founded the Khalji line in Malwa.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a dynastic founder from later members bearing the same family name.
accepted.sec: Malwa - rulers, Mandu monuments → builder (Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Jami Masjid), Baz Bahadur and Rupmati

accepted.s: Hoshang Shah’s Tomb at Mandu is significant because it is regarded as:
o: The first fort built by Akbar
The first covered courtyard mosque in the Deccan
accepted.x: Hoshang Shah’s Tomb is regarded as India’s first marble tomb.
accepted.tq: Match the monument with its distinguishing architectural feature.
accepted.sec: Malwa - rulers, Mandu monuments → builder (Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Jami Masjid), Baz Bahadur and Rupmati

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding monuments at Mandu:
1. Hoshang Shah began the Jami Masjid.
2. Mahmud Khalji completed the Jami Masjid.
3. Ghiyasuddin Khalji built the Hindola Mahal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Hoshang Shah began the Jami Masjid, Mahmud Khalji completed it, and Ghiyasuddin Khalji built the Hindola Mahal.
accepted.tq: Break a monument’s construction history into builder and completer roles.
accepted.sec: Malwa - rulers, Mandu monuments → builder (Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Jami Masjid), Baz Bahadur and Rupmati

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Jami Masjid was begun by Hoshang Shah and completed by Mahmud Khalji, not by Baz Bahadur. The other three pairs are correct.
accepted.tq: Find the monument assigned to a ruler from the wrong period.
accepted.sec: Malwa - rulers, Mandu monuments → builder (Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Jami Masjid), Baz Bahadur and Rupmati

accepted.s:
Which of the following monuments belong to the late Malwa period?
1. Baz Bahadur’s Palace
2. Rupmati’s Pavilion
3. Ashrafi Mahal
4. Hoshang Shah’s Tomb
accepted.x: Baz Bahadur’s Palace, Rupmati’s Pavilion and Ashrafi Mahal belong to the late Malwa period. Hoshang Shah’s Tomb is associated with Hoshang Shah.
accepted.tq: Separate a period-based group from an earlier monument.
accepted.sec: Malwa - rulers, Mandu monuments → builder (Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Jami Masjid), Baz Bahadur and Rupmati

accepted.s: Who was the last Sultan of Malwa and was defeated by Akbar?
accepted.x: Baz Bahadur was the last Sultan of Malwa. He was defeated by Akbar and is associated with his romance with Rupmati.
accepted.tq: Match the last ruler with the conqueror and associated cultural memory.
accepted.sec: Malwa - rulers, Mandu monuments → builder (Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Jami Masjid), Baz Bahadur and Rupmati

accepted.s: Which ruler of Gujarat founded Ahmedabad in 1411 on the banks of the Sabarmati?
accepted.x: Ahmad Shah I founded Ahmedabad in 1411 on the Sabarmati River.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–city–date association.
accepted.sec: Gujarat Sultanate rulers → contribution (Ahmad Shah, Mahmud Begarha, Bahadur Shah), Mirat-i-Sikandari

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Zafar Khan — founder of the Gujarat Sultanate
2. Ahmad Shah I — founded Ahmedabad
3. Mahmud Begarha — captured Girnar and Champaner
4. Bahadur Shah — annexed Malwa
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Zafar Khan, also called Muzaffar Shah I, founded the Gujarat Sultanate; Ahmad Shah founded Ahmedabad; Mahmud Begarha captured Girnar and Champaner; and Bahadur Shah annexed Malwa.
accepted.tq: Check each ruler against his principal contribution before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Gujarat Sultanate rulers → contribution (Ahmad Shah, Mahmud Begarha, Bahadur Shah), Mirat-i-Sikandari

accepted.s: Mahmud Begarha’s name is associated with the capture of which two forts?
accepted.x: Mahmud Begarha captured Girnar in Junagadh and Champaner, the two forts associated with his name.
accepted.tq: Test the ruler–two-forts association using nearby regional monuments as distractors.
accepted.sec: Gujarat Sultanate rulers → contribution (Ahmad Shah, Mahmud Begarha, Bahadur Shah), Mirat-i-Sikandari

accepted.s: Mahmud Begarha joined Egypt against the Portuguese in which context?
o: The campaigns at Chaul and Diu
The annexation of Malwa and attack on Chittor
The conquest of Girnar and Champaner
The foundation of Ahmedabad and Burhanpur
accepted.x: Mahmud Begarha joined Egypt against the Portuguese in the context of Chaul in 1508 and the defeat at Diu in 1509.
accepted.tq: Link a ruler with the correct foreign power and maritime campaign.
accepted.sec: Gujarat Sultanate rulers → contribution (Ahmad Shah, Mahmud Begarha, Bahadur Shah), Mirat-i-Sikandari

accepted.s:
Which of the following events is associated with Bahadur Shah of Gujarat?
1. Annexation of Malwa in 1531
2. Attack on Chittor in 1535
3. Defeat by Humayun
4. Death at Diu in 1537
accepted.x: Bahadur Shah annexed Malwa in 1531, attacked Chittor in 1535, was defeated by Humayun and was killed by the Portuguese at Diu in 1537.
accepted.tq: Recognise a complete sequence of events in one ruler’s career.
accepted.sec: Gujarat Sultanate rulers → contribution (Ahmad Shah, Mahmud Begarha, Bahadur Shah), Mirat-i-Sikandari

accepted.s: The Gujarat Sultanate was annexed by Akbar in:
accepted.x: Akbar annexed Gujarat in 1572.
accepted.tq: Distinguish imperial annexation from earlier regional conquests and dates.
accepted.sec: Gujarat Sultanate rulers → contribution (Ahmad Shah, Mahmud Begarha, Bahadur Shah), Mirat-i-Sikandari

accepted.s: Who authored the Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate titled Mirat-i-Sikandari?
accepted.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari was written by Sikandar bin Muhammad as a Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an author’s name from a similarly named ruler or chronicle.
accepted.sec: Gujarat Sultanate rulers → contribution (Ahmad Shah, Mahmud Begarha, Bahadur Shah), Mirat-i-Sikandari

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Chronicle)
 a. Mirat-i-Sikandari
 b. Burhan-i-Maasir
 c. Riyaz-us-Salatin
 d. Riyaz-ul-Insha

List-II (Subject)
 i. Bengal
 ii. Mahmud Gawan’s letters
 iii. Gujarat
 iv. Ahmadnagar
accepted.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari concerns Gujarat, Burhan-i-Maasir concerns Ahmadnagar, Riyaz-us-Salatin concerns Bengal, and Riyaz-ul-Insha contains Mahmud Gawan’s letters.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure chronicle–region pair and complete the one-to-one matching.
accepted.sec: Gujarat Sultanate rulers → contribution (Ahmad Shah, Mahmud Begarha, Bahadur Shah), Mirat-i-Sikandari

accepted.s: Who founded the Faruqi kingdom of Khandesh in 1382?
accepted.x: Malik Raja Faruqi founded the Faruqi kingdom in 1382 in the Khandesh region.
accepted.tq: Match the founder with the correct regional kingdom.
accepted.sec: Minor regional kingdoms → founder + region (Faruqis of Khandesh, Sisodia and Rathore chiefs)

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Faruqi kingdom is correct?
1. Its capital was Burhanpur.
2. It was located in Khandesh in the Tapti valley.
3. Its fort of Asirgarh was taken by Akbar in 1601.
accepted.x: Burhanpur was the capital of the Faruqi kingdom, which lay in Khandesh’s Tapti valley; Akbar took Asirgarh in 1601.
accepted.tq: Combine capital, region and later imperial conquest in one regional-kingdom question.
accepted.sec: Minor regional kingdoms → founder + region (Faruqis of Khandesh, Sisodia and Rathore chiefs)

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Sisodias — Mewar
2. Rathores — Marwar
3. Faruqis — Khandesh
4. Sisodias — Tapti valley
accepted.x: Sisodias were associated with Mewar, Rathores with Marwar and Faruqis with Khandesh. The Tapti valley was associated with Khandesh, not the Sisodias.
accepted.tq: Use region-based elimination to distinguish neighbouring Rajput and Deccan kingdoms.
accepted.sec: Minor regional kingdoms → founder + region (Faruqis of Khandesh, Sisodia and Rathore chiefs)

accepted.s: Which ruler is associated with the Vijay Stambha at Chittor and Kumbhalgarh?
accepted.x: Rana Kumbha of the Sisodia line is associated with the Vijay Stambha at Chittor and Kumbhalgarh.
accepted.tq: Match a regional ruler with his architectural contributions.
accepted.sec: Minor regional kingdoms → founder + region (Faruqis of Khandesh, Sisodia and Rathore chiefs)

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Rathores?
1. Rao Jodha founded Jodhpur in 1459.
2. Rao Bika founded Bikaner.
3. The Rathore chiefs were associated with Marwar.
Option_a_placeholder
accepted.x: Rao Jodha founded Jodhpur in 1459, Rao Bika founded Bikaner, and the Rathores were associated with Marwar.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–city–region combination to verify all three statements.
accepted.sec: Minor regional kingdoms → founder + region (Faruqis of Khandesh, Sisodia and Rathore chiefs)
